artworks.title: East pediment of the Temple of Zeus at Olympia (central group)
artworks.description: Olympia's east pediment — Zeus between Oenomaus and Pelops before the fatal chariot race for Hippodamia.

artworks.title: Pelops and Hippodamia
artworks.description: Kaselowsky's academic race aftermath — Pelops with Hippodamia, the bride won by Myrtilus' sabotage.

artworks.title: Terracotta plaque with King Oinomaos and his charioteer
artworks.description: Roman plaque of King Oenomaus and his charioteer — the Pisa tyrant whose races killed suitors until Pelops came.

artworks.title: Oenomaus and Myrtilus
artworks.description: Relief of Oenomaus and Myrtilus — the charioteer whose treachery and curse seed the Atreid doom.

artworks.title: Pelops mosaic (Noheda)
artworks.description: Noheda mosaic — late Roman Pelops still racing across a villa floor, the Olympia myth in tesserae.

popCulture.title: Olympic Games
popCulture.description: Tradition ties the chariot race for Hippodamia to Olympia's founding — Pelops' cursed victory as the mythic seed of the Games.

popCulture.title: Pelops
popCulture.description: Pelops endures as the ivory-shouldered ancestor of the Atreids — the race that won a bride and doomed a dynasty.
